NodeService owns AI receivers and clears them before js_env teardown. Receiver destruction order protects JS callbacks; removing storage/clear as duplicate cleanup would change lifetime.
Destroyable foreign receiver field-count guard prevents reading cppgc layout as legacy pointer. Must retain guard on user-callable receiver conversion.

NetLog stop rejects when Mojo drops its reply rather than retaining unresolved promise. Drop handler is an externally observable settlement guarantee; no native network-service teardown test available.
MessagePort checks entanglement again after JS serialization, which may execute getters and close the port. Repeated check protects a distinct reentrancy boundary.
JSChunkedDataPipeGetter aborts repeated StartReading rather than replacing active pipe state. Must preserve single active read and terminal settlement.

Menu changes retain native menu/model lifetimes across Mac/views/GTK/X11/tray calls and guard JS insert state. These are cross-platform ownership protections; native callback reentrancy remains untested.
ImportedSharedTexture deletion and release callback are posted to owning sequence. Keep task runner ownership and posted release; inline cleanup could run on arbitrary refcount-release thread.
MSIX update, TouchID and media promises settle on UI sequence. Captures own promises through callbacks; do not inline thread hops without proving callback sequence.

WebFrameMain adopts current RFH before reentrant exposure and destroys wrappers for WebContents teardown. Registry and owning WebContents boundaries matter; pending native navigation/destruction proof.
WebFrame argument getters run before RenderFrame lookup; frame may disappear while getters execute. Retain lookup after conversion rather than cache stale frame.

Notification::Close rechecks the weak platform notification after Dismiss may run JS; Show returns if reentrant close listener already created a notification. This prevents orphaning a platform delegate. Native notification reentrancy unexecuted.
Linux portal shortcut cleanup ignores stale unregistration after registration is gone. Registry lookup protects asynchronous reply ordering; portal runtime unavailable on this host.
UtilityProcess launch failure cleans up/unpins and emits exit; FD transfer uses ownership exchange. Reviewed failure and success transitions; crash/failed-exec native test required.
ServiceWorker uses registry ownership and discards redundant nonrunning wrappers. Persistent service worker and stop/destruction transitions require Electron execution.
XDG utility callback settles even in no-wait mode. Do not omit completion merely because process output is not awaited.
Warning emission chooses current isolate with renderer fallback; browser-isolate assumption fails in renderer paths. Native renderer warning execution unavailable.
Reply channel serializes before consuming callback, then rechecks callback after reentrancy. Moving callback first loses reply on conversion failure; removing second check permits double reply.
Data-pipe holder destructor erases weak registry entry; weak lookup must not retain stale holder identity after GC. Requires GC/native pipe execution.
Debugger destructor detaches host and suppresses late messages. Detach is part of teardown protocol, not incidental cleanup.
Sharder formatting precedes per-job weights change; deterministic packing remains. Later executable fixture covers actual successor script, not claimed as exact-parent runtime proof.
